name: Naturalization

requirements.blocker_text: Requires 10 consecutive years of residence in Egypt (Article 4).
Must be of sound mind without being a societal burden, of good conduct with no criminal convictions, proficient in Arabic, and have a legitimate source of income.
Persons of Egyptian origin need only 5 years of ordinary residence (Article 4), plus the same conduct/income/language conditions as the standard route.

requirement_groups.name: Born in Egypt to foreign parents from an Arab or Muslim-majority country

requirements.blocker_text: A person born in Egypt to foreign parents from an Arabic-speaking or Muslim-majority country may apply after just 1 year of residence (Article 4).
The President may grant citizenship by decree without the standard restrictions to a person who has rendered honorable services to Egypt, or who leads an Egyptian religious organization (Article 5).

evidence_required.document: Proof of residence period matching the applicable category

sources.title: Egypt -- Law No. 26 of 1975 Concerning Egyptian Nationality (official English translation, verbatim primary legislation text), Article 4: 10-year standard residence, 5-year Egyptian-origin route, 1-year route for those born in Egypt to Arab/Muslim-majority-country parents; Article 5: exceptional presidential grant

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Egypt). Treated the africanchildforum.org-hosted English translation as tier 1: it presents itself as a direct translation of the primary legislation text rather than a summary, consistent with this dataset's convention for verbatim-legislation mirrors on non-.gov domains. IMPORTANT CAVEAT: this specific document is the ORIGINAL 1975 text and does NOT incorporate the 2004 amendment (Law 154/2004) -- however, that amendment's confirmed substantive changes (per secondary academic sourcing, see eg_citizenship_by_descent.json's notes) affected descent/nationality-by-birth provisions (Articles 2-3), not the naturalization residence-duration figures in Article 4 used here, so this file's core figures are not believed to be affected by that gap. Still, flagging explicitly that a post-2004-amendment consolidated text was not independently verified for Article 4 specifically. dual_citizenship_allowed modeled true based on the general absence of an explicit renunciation requirement in the extracted naturalization provisions -- not an explicit statutory statement either way, flagged as an inference.
